\chapter{Market, Beach, Garden, Corner, Turn}
\label{ch:ka-market-beach-garden-corner-turn}
\hlchaptermodality{110}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say a market, a beach, a garden, a corner and a turn, then locate a bird or school relative to a named tree or house.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 110: I can use short, fixed on/under/near/far/inside place frames with a named reference.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸಂತೆ} (sante)}{ಸಂತೆ (sante)}]{\kn{ಸಂತೆ} (sante) — a market}

\label{lesson:KA-C110-sante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a library, then a bank. Recall “I go to school” with \textbf{\kn{ಶಾಲೆಗೆ}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸಂತೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸಂತೆ}} — \emph{sante} — \textquotedblleft{}a market\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\kn{ಸಂತೆ}} (\emph{sante}) is uncertain. Neither DEDR nor CDIAL records it, and no source for it is settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sante}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sante}
  \item \emph{Recall:} \textbf{\kn{ನಾನು} \kn{ಶಾಲೆಗೆ} \kn{ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ}} — “I go to school.”
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a library, then the Kannada for a bank, then say \emph{sante} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ} \kn{ಹಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಇದೆ}. (marada mēle hakki ide)}{ಮರದ ಮೇಲೆ ಹಕ್ಕಿ ಇದೆ. (marada mēle hakki ide)}]{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ} / \kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಕೆಳಗೆ} — on or under the tree}

\label{lesson:KA-C110-tree-on-under}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{\kn{ಮರ}} (\emph{mara}, tree) and \textbf{\kn{ಹಕ್ಕಿ}} (\emph{hakki}, bird). Point up for \textbf{\kn{ಮೇಲೆ}} (\emph{mēle}, on top), then down for \textbf{\kn{ಕೆಳಗೆ}} (\emph{keḷage}, under). You know all four words already.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: on the tree}
Listen once. Follow the printed line with your finger:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ} \kn{ಹಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{marada mēle hakki ide.} — The bird is on the tree.
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಮರದ}} (\emph{marada}) means “of the tree” here. It names what \textbf{\kn{ಮೇಲೆ}} is relative to. Keep \textbf{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ}} together as “on the tree”; \textbf{\kn{ಹಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಇದೆ}} says that the bird is there. This one frame does not teach every Kannada noun ending.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar lens: under the tree}]
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಕೆಳಗೆ} \kn{ಹಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{marada keḷage hakki ide.} — The bird is under the tree.
\end{quote}

The tree and bird stay the same. Only \textbf{\kn{ಮೇಲೆ}} changes to \textbf{\kn{ಕೆಳಗೆ}}. Read both lines aloud, slowly. Listen for the word that tells you where.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn: on or under}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} The bird is \textbf{on} the tree.
  \item \emph{Say it:} The bird is \textbf{under} the tree.
  \item \emph{Point to:} which printed line puts the bird below?
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Writing: the place phrases}
\emph{Write it:} \textbf{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ}} and \textbf{\kn{ಮರದ} \kn{ಕೆಳಗೆ}} from memory. Check the two final words against the lines above.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say “on the tree” and “under the tree” once more. You have located one named thing relative to another. Direction words alone do not give that reference.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ} \kn{ಮನೆಯ} \kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ} \kn{ಇದೆ}. (śāle maneya …)}{ಶಾಲೆ ಮನೆಯ ಹತ್ತಿರ ಇದೆ. (śāle maneya …)}]{\kn{ಮನೆಯ} \kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ} / \kn{ಮನೆಯಿಂದ} \kn{ದೂರ} / \kn{ಮನೆಯೊಳಗೆ}}

\label{lesson:KA-C110-house-near-far-inside}



\begin{quote}
Recall the chapter's five place words: market, beach, garden, corner, turn. Say them before checking: \textbf{\kn{ಸಂತೆ}}, \textbf{\kn{ಕಡಲತೀರ}}, \textbf{\kn{ತೋಟ}}, \textbf{\kn{ಮೂಲೆ}}, \textbf{\kn{ತಿರುವು}}. Now say “on the tree” and “under the tree”. Recall \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆ}} (\emph{mane}, house), \textbf{\kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ}} (\emph{hattira}, near), and \textbf{\kn{ದೂರ}} (\emph{dūra}, far). We will keep one house as the reference and change its relation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: near the house}
Listen, then read:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ} \kn{ಮನೆಯ} \kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{śāle maneya hattira ide.} — The school is near the house.
\end{quote}

You know \textbf{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ}} (\emph{śāle}, school). \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯ}} (\emph{maneya}) links the house to \textbf{\kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ}}. Say \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯ} \kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ}} as one place phrase.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar lens: far from the house}]
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ} \kn{ಮನೆಯಿಂದ} \kn{ದೂರ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{śāle maneyinda dūra ide.} — The school is far from the house.
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯಿಂದ}} (\emph{maneyinda}) means “from the house”; its \textbf{-\kn{ಇಂದ}} is the same source marker you met in \textbf{\kn{ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನಿಂದ}}. Do not put \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯ}} in this far-from line. Listen to near and far once more; answer aloud which one means “far from the house”.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: inside the house}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಹಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಮನೆಯೊಳಗೆ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hakki maneyoḷage ide.} — The bird is inside the house.
\end{quote}

Here \textbf{\kn{ಒಳಗೆ}} (\emph{oḷage}) means “inside”. In this fixed place phrase it joins \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯ}} as \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯೊಳಗೆ}}. Listen and point: is the bird on the tree, under the tree, or inside the house?

\begin{cousinweb}
You heard \textbf{\kn{ಒಳಗೆ}} earlier in \textbf{\kn{ಒಳಗೆ} \kn{ಬನ್ನಿ}} (“please come in”). It is native Dravidian for “inside”; DEDR 698 also lists Tamil \emph{uḷ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn: three house relations}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} The school is near the house; now far from the house.
  \item \emph{Say it:} The bird is inside the house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the line that puts the bird \textbf{under} the tree.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Writing: three house phrases}
\emph{Write it:} \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯ} \kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ}}, \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯಿಂದ} \kn{ದೂರ}}, and \textbf{\kn{ಮನೆಯೊಳಗೆ}} from memory; check each against the printed examples.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Name the five places: near, far, on, under, inside. For each, say the \textbf{complete phrase} with its tree or house reference. That is what you will retrieve later; isolated words are not enough.
\end{tcolorbox}
